correctness.rationale: Every private-leaf arm must contain a selected vertex. The three remaining states are exhaustive; core-only arms demand no adjacent leaf-only arm because their omitted leaf has a unique possible witness. Conversely each omitted core on a leaf-only arm is witnessed privately by its selected leaf. This proves the exact reflexive-P3 homomorphism bijection and size weights, so each induced component receives two monochromatic options and gives the displayed polynomial for all finite base graphs. Its near-minimum coefficient follows from subsets U of size n-1. The #P reduction is parsimonious and uses Dyer–Greenhill Theorems 1.1–1.2, explicitly proven for subcubic WR inputs. `verify.py` direct private-neighbor tests compared with two independent count constructions on 183 finite graphs and passed; finite tests are not substituted for proof.

originality.rationale: The retained result is not the already established Widom–Rowlinson partition formula or its #P-completeness, and not the known minimum count 2^{c(H)}. Its new bridge is an exact all-super-dominating-set interpretation of the known spin model for arbitrary graph bases, which transfers #P-completeness to bounded-degree leaf coronas and yields a cut-vertex coefficient. value.rationale: An exact full-cardinality classification on the natural corona product family is mathematically more informative than the easy minimum number and 2^{c(H)} optimum count. The cut-vertex coefficient connects the second domination coefficient to base graph connectivity. The parsimonious bijection proves #P-completeness for all-set counting even with maximum degree four, making a sharp algorithmic distinction within a strongly restricted infinite graph class. A known WR polynomial alone has a different domain and does not explain this domination phenomenon.
